data.name: Shanmuga
data.gender_notes: Shanmuga is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: God of War with Six Faces
data.long_meaning: Shanmuga is a name of Lord Murugan, also known as Kartikeya or Subramaniam. He is the god of war, wisdom, and knowledge. He is depicted with six heads, representing the six aspects of consciousness. Each head represents an aspect: peace, war, creation, preservation, destruction, and wisdom. The name Shanmuga carries the meaning “God of War with Six Faces” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Tamil, Sanskrit. Parents who choose Shanmuga usually hope their child will grow to embody god of war with six faces and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Shanmuga represents the divine power of protection and wisdom. He is the embodiment of courage, loyalty, and victory. He helps us to overcome obstacles and challenges in our lives, and to find inner peace and wisdom.
data.etymology: Shanmuga belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of War with Six Faces.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shanmuga total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Shanmuga, also known as Lord Murugan or Kartikeya, is a major Hindu deity worshipped across Tamil Nadu, South India, and in other parts of India with significant Tamil influences. Shanmuga is revered as the god of war, wisdom, and knowledge. His six heads represent the various aspects of human life and consciousness. Shanmuga is often worshipped to attain victory, knowledge, and to ask for protection.
data.spiritual_significance: Shanmuga, as a manifestation of Lord Murugan, is a symbol of divine power and wisdom. The six heads represent the six aspects of consciousness: Kala (time), Gnana (knowledge), Saranaagathi (grace), Prema (love), Warrier (warrior), and Peace. This name reminds us of the importance of seeking wisdom and knowledge in life, maintaining inner peace, and having a warrior spirit to face the challenges that come our way. It also highlights the importance of seeking divine protection and grace in times of need.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shanmuga symbolizes the six faces of Lord Subrahmanyan, representing wisdom, compassion, courage, generosity, beauty, and destruction of ignorance. His six arms hold various weapons, affirming his role as a protector and healer.
